newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt court sentences five to death for killings.
newsitem.headline: Egypt court sentences five to death for killings.

text.p: An Egyptian state security court on Monday sentenced five suspected Moslem militants to death, two of them in their absence.
The five were among a group of 32 people who were charged with killing ten policemen and ten civilians in the town of Assiut in southern Egypt in 1993.
Security sources had said, when they went on trial in March, that the men were alleged members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) and were arrested almost two years ago.
They had also been charged with bombing several buildings in the southern city, the sources added.
Prosecutors had accused the men of belonging to the military wing of the illegal Gama'a and of waging the attacks from December 1993 to April 1994, which included shooting at a passenger train.
The Gama'a, Egypt's largest militant organisation, has since 1992 waged a campaign to topple the government of President Hosni Mubarak and establish a purist Islamist state.
More than 1,000 people have died and hundreds have been wounded since the Gama'a took up arms against the government. Egypt has since carried out more than 40 executions.
